memory_lessons.applicability: Use these complete-call results as contrasts for forward/input-gradient fusion; they do not identify the cause of timing differences.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline measured 35.464 ms, prior same-thread fusion measured 34.929 ms, and the path-specialized block-cohort fusion measured 36.408 ms. Fusion's launch reduction alone does not establish a speedup.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the shared-tile fused candidate against the same complete-call baseline and verify all correctness cases.

proposal.hypothesis: The measured same-thread fusion was correct at 34.929 ms versus the 35.464 ms baseline, while a one-launch variant using separate block cohorts measured 36.408 ms. This experiment keeps same-thread fusion but cooperatively stages each block's x and gy halo plus filter in shared memory. That should reduce repeated global loads and per-tap bounds checks for the shared-memory-sized path; staging overhead, synchronization, or resource pressure may outweigh the savings. Larger filters use a fused global-memory fallback so correctness does not depend on shared-memory capacity. This candidate has not been measured.

retained: Replace separate forward and input-gradient launches with one fused kernel that accumulates and freshly writes y and gx for each output element.
For filters fitting within the bounded shared-memory allocation, cooperatively stage x and gy tile halos plus the filter; rely on zero-filled halo elements instead of per-tap bounds checks.
Use a fused global-memory path when the shared-memory requirement exceeds 8 KiB, preserving the operation for larger filters without depending on device-specific shared-memory capacity.
Leave the weight-gradient kernel and launch unchanged.
